stories.headline: The United States put 50% tariffs on $20 billion of Canadian goods after trade talks collapsed
stories.body:
The United States put 50% tariffs on $20 billion worth of Canadian goods on Saturday. US President Donald Trump first announced the 50% tariffs on July 20. Trump said the reason was Canadian bans on the sale of US alcohol in provincial stores.

The tariffs affect about $20 billion of Canadian imports. This amount represents about 5% of total Canadian exports. Canadian exports to the US totaled $409 billion last year. Those exports accounted for 73 percent of all Canadian exports. Canadian Federation of Independent Business president Dan Kelly gave an estimate about the impact. Kelly estimated that 40% of small Canadian exporters will be directly hit by the US tariffs.

Trade talks between the two countries collapsed. After the talks collapsed, Trump wrote a message on social media. Trump wrote that Canada wants the benefits of being a US state without being one. Trump also spoke on Fox News. Trump said Canadians were foolish to engage in a trade war with the US. He said Canadians are foolish to think they will win.

US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer spoke on Saturday. Greer said there are no plans to resume trade talks with Canada. Canada and Mexico formally requested a 16-year renewal of the USMCA trade pact this summer. But Trump refused to renew the USMCA trade agreement.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney pledged to respond to the US tariffs. Carney promised to match US tariffs dollar for dollar starting September 8. The Canadian tariffs will cover items including steel, dairy, appliances, and electronics.

Carney said US negotiators made threats during trade talks. Carney said they made threats against the French language, Quebec culture, and Canadian culture. Carney also visited China in January. During that visit, Carney agreed to reduce tariffs on a capped number of Chinese electric vehicles. In exchange, China lowered its duties on Canadian canola.

Donald Trump initially announced 50% tariffs on July 20, citing Canadian bans on the sale of US alcohol in provincial stores.
The 50% US tariffs affect approximately $20 billion of Canadian imports, representing about 5% of total Canadian exports.
Canadian exports to the US totaled $409 billion last year, accounting for 73 percent of all Canadian exports.
Canadian Federation of Independent Business president Dan Kelly estimated that 40% of small Canadian exporters will be directly hit by the US tariffs.
US President Donald Trump wrote on social media that Canada wants the benefits of being a State without being one after trade talks collapsed.
US President Donald Trump stated on Fox News that Canadians were foolish to engage in a trade war with the US and think they will win.
US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer stated on Saturday that there are no plans to resume trade talks with Canada.
Donald Trump refused to renew the USMCA trade pact this summer after Canada and Mexico formally requested a 16-year renewal.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney pledged to match US tariffs dollar for dollar starting September 8 on items including steel, dairy, appliances, and electronics.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney stated that US negotiators made threats against the French language, Quebec culture, and Canadian culture.

During a January visit to China, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney agreed to reduce tariffs on a capped number of Chinese electric vehicles in exchange for lowered Chinese duties on Canadian canola.

stories.headline: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned against holding national elections during the war
stories.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that holding elections during the war is a huge risk. Zelenskyy said elections would be a tsunami for the state that will split Ukraine. Ukraine suspended national elections under martial law after Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022. Zelenskyy's five-year presidential term formally expired in May 2024.

Ousted former Ukrainian defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov publicly called for Ukraine to organize fresh elections despite the ongoing war. Fedorov spoke in a BBC interview. Fedorov said Zelenskyy should face questions regarding his awareness of potential inner-circle corruption. His comment came after a money laundering investigation. Ukraine's anti-corruption bureau uncovered a scheme misappropriating more than $3 million in Ukrainian currency. The money was used to pay bail for a former energy minister accused of money laundering.

Zelenskyy also discussed military concerns. Zelenskyy said Russia has a stockpile of between 600 and 630 high-speed ballistic missiles. He said Russia seeks to produce over 100 a month. Zelenskyy said he believes Russia will try to conscript an additional 300,000 soldiers after its parliamentary elections in September.

Foreign allies announced plans to send aid to Ukraine. Germany agreed to supply Ukraine with about 600 PAC-2 and PAC-3 interceptors in 2027 and 2028. Norway announced plans to give 85 billion Norwegian crowns in financial support in the 2027 fiscal year. That support equals $9.2 billion.

Germany agreed to supply Ukraine with about 600 PAC-2 and PAC-3 interceptors in 2027 and 2028.

stories.headline: Iran announced a major natural gas discovery in Fars province containing recoverable energy reserves
stories.body:
Iran announced the discovery of more than 200 billion cubic metres of natural gas in Fars province. Officials said over 160 billion cubic metres of the gas is potentially recoverable. Iranian Oil Minister Mohsen Paknejad spoke about the discovery. Paknejad said the discovery contains more than 7.5 trillion cubic feet of gas. He said around 5.7 trillion cubic feet of that gas is recoverable. Paknejad described the newly discovered gas as sweet. He said low levels of hydrogen sulphide will lower development and operating costs.

The discovery comes after damage to Iranian energy facilities. Attacks on Iranian energy infrastructure started in late February. The attacks reduced Iran's daily gas production capacity by around a quarter. Iran's pre-war natural gas production was estimated at about 650 million cubic metres per day.

Political tensions remain high in the region. US President Donald Trump shared a graphic on Truth Social. The graphic depicted the Strait of Hormuz as new US territory. Iranian Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezaei issued a warning to nearby countries. Rezaei warned neighboring countries that Iran will consider them enemies if they join the US economic war.

Iranian Oil Minister Mohsen Paknejad stated that the new natural gas discovery in Fars province contains more than 7.5 trillion cubic feet of gas, with around 5.7 trillion cubic feet recoverable.
Iranian Oil Minister Mohsen Paknejad described the newly discovered gas as sweet, indicating low levels of hydrogen sulphide that will lower development and operating costs.

Iran's pre-war natural gas production was estimated at approximately 650 million cubic metres per day.

stories.headline: Panama-flagged cargo ship sinks in Bay of Bengal off Odisha coast triggering rescue operation
stories.body:
A Panama-flagged bulk carrier named M.V. Ocean Winner sank in the Bay of Bengal off the coast of Odisha. M.V. Ocean Winner sank about 230 to 240 nautical miles off the coast. The ship was carrying 72,100 metric tonnes of iron ore. The vessel departed Paradip Port late on August 20, 2026. Specifically, the ship departed the Paradip coast at 10:42 pm on August 20. The vessel was carrying iron ore fines.

Initial reports from Indian maritime authorities said M.V. Ocean Winner was bound for China. But other government information indicated Singapore as its destination. Communication with M.V. Ocean Winner was lost 36 hours after its departure. The loss of communication prompted a search and rescue request to the Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre. Victory Star Group Co Ltd requested search and rescue assistance after communication was lost late on August 22.

The Andaman & Nicobar Command reported that M.V. Ocean Winner sent a distress alert on Saturday. The alert came from a position around 300 nautical miles north-northwest of Diglipur. M.V. Ocean Winner had 24 crew members onboard. The crew comprised 20 Chinese nationals, three Myanmarese nationals, and one Bangladeshi national.

An Indian Navy P8I surveillance aircraft detected two floating liferafts near the reported position of M.V. Ocean Winner. The aircraft also spotted an oil slick in the area. Commercial vessel MT Aisopos rescued two Chinese crew members from liferafts by late evening on August 22, 2026. Union Shipping and Waterways Minister Sarbananda Sonowal confirmed that two survivors were rescued. Sonowal said the rescued crew received medical care.

The search operation for the missing crew members continues. The Indian Coast Guard deployed vessels ICGS Varad, ICGS Anmol, and ICGS Vijit to assist in search operations. Coast Guard spokesperson Commandant Amit Uniyal reported that rough sea conditions were slowing work. Uniyal said rough sea conditions in the Bay of Bengal were hampering search operations.

Database records from Equasis show M.V. Ocean Winner was a 28-year-old vessel built in 1998. The vessel measured 225 metres long and 32.26 metres wide. It had a capacity of around 73,000 tonnes. M.V. Ocean Winner's current owner is based in Fujian, China. Protection and Indemnity insurance covered the vessel starting August 1, 2026. An inspection in Chittagong, Bangladesh, in June reported three deficiencies. One deficiency involved its magnetic compass.

Similar maritime incidents have happened in Indian waters before. In September 2009, the Mongolian-flagged bulk carrier MV Black Rose sank near Paradip. That vessel sank after developing a hull leak while carrying 23,847 tonnes of iron ore. In 2009, the MV Asian Forest capsized off Mangalore Port on India's west coast. That ship capsized due to cargo liquefaction after loading iron ore fines.
